outcome.answer:
For linear-time long-context recall, the Raven paper directly targets the recall problem by changing how a linear model writes to memory: it uses a fixed set of memory slots and learned input-dependent routing so only a selected subset of slots is decayed/updated at each step, aiming to preserve long-range content while avoiding interference from dense state updates and avoiding SWA’s fixed-window eviction. It reports strong long-context recall on recall-intensive benchmarks and effectiveness when extrapolating to much longer contexts. [1]

If you specifically want the “linear attention” route, Kaczmarz Linear Attention (KLA) modifies a delta-rule linear recurrent attention approach by deriving a key-norm-normalized step size for residual updates, aiming to improve accuracy, extrapolation, and decode efficiency while keeping the recurrent state shape and linear recurrence structure. [2]

These differ from Adaptive Memory Decay for Log-Linear Attention, which focuses on making the Fenwick-tree hierarchy’s decay parameter input-dependent (via an MLP) to adapt memory weighting by content while preserving log-linear complexity. [3]
